newsitem.title: UK: Euro crude outlook - Output crimped by maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Euro crude outlook - Output crimped by maintenance.

text.p: North Sea crudes are likely to firm this week, with the release of June loading programmes expected to flag a drop in output next month, traders said.
Summer maintenance at North Sea oil installations is expected to eat heavily into June loadings.
"We are expecting thinner loading programmes (for June) and sellers are getting bullish and asking higher prices," said one North Sea trader.
June Brent gained some sixty cents late last week, while CFD trade for this week valued Dated Brent at June Brent -12 cents, more than 20 cents up on the last deal done.

A Reuters survey of U.K. and Norwegian North Sea maintenance programmes showed that scheduled shutdowns would claim 350,000 to 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of production in June, or 21 to 27 standard 500,000 barrel cargoes.
This compares to a loss of 150,000 to 200,000 bpd or nine to 12 cargoes from the May loading programmes due to maintenance.
The Forties loading programme is expected to be particularly light in early June, while Brent and Norwegian Oseberg are also set to be hit.
"There are short-term signs that the market is going to be tighter and that is sure to help prices up," said one trader.

Demand from U.S. Gulf refiners looking to fill the gap left by West African barrels which have headed in droves to the Far East this month could mop up much of the remaining May supplies, traders said.
At least three million May-loading North Sea barrels have already been fixed to head trans-Atlantic.
But the heavy Far East buying of West African crudes may start to wane as June sales get under way if the Brent/Dubai spread starts to widen from recent lows, traders said.
"June barrels have already started to head east, but most of those are baseload rather than incremental supplies," said one.
Short covering on Dubai intermonth spreads early last week quickly stoked the market, pushing it firmly into backwardation, and sharply narrowing the Brent/Dubai spread.
June Brent/Dubai shed over $1.00 a barrel in a week to just 30 to 40 cents, but began to ease later in the week as Brent rallied.
"The way the (Brent/Dubai) spread was earlier in the week, Dated related purchases were extremely attractive to Far East buyers," said one trader on Friday.
"But it looks to me that the spread's going to have to come in or the market which is already long on oil is going to get more than it needs."

Nevertheless, at least two spot cargoes of June-loading Angolan Cabindas have already found homes in the Far East and South Korean refiners are still interested in Nigerian Bonny Light, with the grade pegged at Dated Brent +50 cents on Friday.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals, recently seen overvalued relative to other regional sours such as Iraqi Kirkuk, may lose further ground this week having fallen some 20 cents to trade at a low of Dated Brent -$1.18 on Friday.
